For those of you playing 5E somewhere other than Faerun: Tell us about your setting!

I guess I'll get the ball rolling.

My group's current campaign has come to an end (well, we're in the middle of a huge-ass fight with an ancient, spell casting dragon that we started in last week's session and will hopefully finish the fight this week), so we'll be starting a new one in a part of my world I hadn't detailed much yet. Before I show off the setting, I'll go over the stuff rules-wise that we've changed to make 5E fit our world better.

  • Dying is easier. We use the Slow Natural Healing rule, for starters. When you're at 0 Hit Points and are making Death Saves, since a natural 20 brings you back up with 1 Hit Point, we've ruled that a natural 1 means you're dead-dead. The rule for dying from massive damage is different, too. Instead of dying if the remainder damage (after being brought to 0) would be equal to or greater than your max Hit Points, you die if remainder damage is greater than whatever your current hit points were when you took the hit that dropped you to 0. Some poisons and situations are "save or die," a la old school D&D. I don't care if you're max level; if you get bitten by a black mamba, there's a damn good chance you will die.

  • Races: There are the usual Dwarf, Elf, Gnome, Halfling, and Human. In addition, there are the Ratten and the Fjothr. The Ratten are a rat-like race that relatively recently became a "good" race. The Fjothr -- bird-like humanoids -- are also a new race, but they're not just new to being good/playable, they actually were created by the gods in recent world history.

  • Classes: Players start at zero level with a Profession (essentially a 5E background). When they gain enough Experience, they hit level 1 and choose from one of the eight classes: Barbarian, Bard, Druid, Goði (cleric), Ranger, Rogue, Warrior, or Zauberer (wizard). The classes themselves are very closely based on the SRD classes, so instead of having forks to choose from at 3rd level, they are the more "traditional" versions of the classes.

  • Levels: Instead of 1-20, characters progress from 0-10. 10th level in our world is roughly the same as 20th level in 5E.

  • Magic: Magic is much less common that btb 5E. Spells are cast with a point system. Each time you level in a class, you gain Magic Points. Bards and Rangers gain 1d4 per level, Goði and Druids gain 1d6 per level, and Zauberers gain 1d10. First level classes have access to "Elementary Spells" (cantrips) which cost 1 MP to cast. After the Elementary spells, there are five "Circles" of spells, with each corresponding to the brb 5E spell levels (First Circle spells are 1st level, Second Circle spells are 2nd level, etc.). Characters of levels 2-3 can cast from the First Circle, 4-5 from the Second Circle, 6-7 from the Third, 8-9 from the Fourth, and 10th from the Fifth. Yes, you read that right. There are no spells higher than 5th level, and you have to be max level to cast them. Once again, magic is much less common.

I think those are the biggest mechanical changes we've made. There are some smaller tweaks here and there, though (for example the Medicine skill and Religion skill have swapped stats; Intelligence for Medicine and Wisdom for Religion).

Now, for the setting information. This is just a portion of our world, but will be where we're starting/focusing for our new campaign.

The Barony of Punchstein makes up the western portion of the Kingdom of Karak on the land of Mithgarthr. Therein is located the town of Reichenbach which is known for its friendly population, for their annual "Kindervolk Glücklichfest", and for the doppelbock ("Ten Scythes") that their largest tavern serves.

http://mithgarthrentertainment.com/uploads/3/4/7/4/34746664/5579537_orig.png

One of five large towns in the Barony of Punchstein, Reichenbach is a peaceful burg situated where the Kleinfluss river meets the Klaarwasser. To the west of Reichenbach is the quaint Reichklein Wald, a small forest used for logging by the folks of Reichenbach. Not much further west rises an arm of the Suderberg mountains known as the Punchstein Crags. To the east is the Klaargabel Wald, a dense old-growth forest generally avoided by common folk. On the other side of the Klaargabel Wald lies Mittplatz, another of the barony's towns which is larger than Reichenbach. The area is bordered to the south by the Klaarwasser, and to the north lie the rolling, lightly wooded hills that the Barony of Punchstein is known for.

http://mithgarthrentertainment.com/uploads/3/4/7/4/34746664/579915_orig.png

Although it is thankfully very rare that the folks of Reichenbach have to deal with the beasts and creatures that call the Klaargabel Wald home, the town is still fortified with a stockade which runs its perimeter and a well-maintained fence encircles the surrounding farmlands. A few small trails run from the town to its closest farmsteads, and the logging trail to the Reichklein Wald is also kept in good repair. Otherwise, there are no proper roads to or from the town. Any travel to the nearest hub of civilization, Mittplatz, is only a short travel by ferry down the Klaarwasser. A small trail does run along the river between the two settlements, but it rarely used since traveling by boat is quicker.

http://mithgarthrentertainment.com/uploads/3/4/7/4/34746664/7886007_orig.png

The land cleared for farming around the town is rich and fertile thanks to the rivers. A good majority of the townsfolk are farmers and goat ranchers, and more than a few fish the river for bass, catfish, and walleye. Reichenbach almost never wants for fresh food. ​ Another common industry in Reichenbach is mining. The foothills of the Punchstein Crags are rich with iron, copper, opal, and to a lesser extent silver. The surrounding hills are pockmarked with old mines. To the locals' lament, they have lost many old mines to foul creatures who have made them their homes. To the more adventuresome types, the old mines sing songs of glory and riches.

  • He was also already personally worth more than a million before he graduated thanks to his 'salary' from the firm.

  • The figures above are inflation adjusted. That "small" $1million loan is not inflated adjusted. That was actually a ~$7 million loan given just before being handed control of a company worth hundreds of millions.

  • By 1990 The Trump Organization, the oversight company managing all of Trump's other estates was billions of dollars in debt. The reason Trump was not entirely wiped out here is that he struck a deal with a huge number of banks enabling him to take out second and even third mortgages on many of his properties. This is just before his bankruptcies to the tune of billions of dollars began.

  • This also isn't even getting into the fact that he was handed these hundreds of millions of dollars just before we entered the biggest bull market in history.
